sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4m in FY2016 to $14,342.9m in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was not smooth: revenue jumped 89.1% in FY2021 to $16,071.7m, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12,172.9m [F6][F7][D241][D292].
The FY2021 spike came from REGEN-COV, which contributed 66.4pp of that year's growth, and its disappearance drove the FY2022 reversal [D582][D585][P43].
Growth has since slowed to 1.0% in FY2025, and the FY2018 and FY2019 figures in the table are later recasts, not the amounts first reported [F10][D440][F3][X3][F4][X4].
The mix has inverted: net product sales fell 17.3% in FY2025 and contributed -9.3pp, while collaboration revenue grew 21.0% and contributed +9.0pp [D506][D507][D522][D523].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% to $2,747.8m on competitive pressure, share loss to compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition [S43][D577][P10].
EYLEA HD partly offset that, rising 36.3% to $1,636.9m on higher volumes [S64][D613][P11].
The largest single driver is now Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits, up 33.6% to $5,241.6m, or 36.5% of revenue, on higher Dupixent sales [S52][D590][D591][P9].
Operating income fell 10.3% while revenue rose 1.0%, so there was no operating leverage in FY2025 [F20][D441][D440].
Operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the FY2021 high of 55.7% [F30][D749][D751][D750].
In FY2025 R&D took 4.7pp off margin as it grew 14.0% to $5,850.2m, or 40.8% of revenue, while SG&A added 2.0pp back [D465][D455][X34][D420][D466].
The SG&A decline of 8.6% was primarily due to lower charitable contributions to Good Days [D456][P5].
Gross margin on net product sales fell partly on manufacturing investment and higher inventory write-offs and reserves [P4].
Net margin held at 31.4% because other income of $1,652.8m offset the operating decline, leaving net income up 2.1% [F50][X117][D442].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9m was 1.11x net income, and free cash flow of $4,080.5m was 0.91x, against a window median of 0.88x [F80][D428][F100][D429][D763].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% sits above the 26.4% window median but well below the 40.6% FY2021 high [D425][D757][D756].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898.4m, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A, as the Tarrytown and Rensselaer build-out continued [F90][D447][D424][D430][P19].
Stock-based compensation of $993.7m equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow, a persistent non-cash add-back [X77][D431].
Net cash reached $16,879.9m, or 117.7% of revenue, against a peer median of -50.7% and in the 100th percentile of eight peers [D434][D435][D781][D780].
Debt is a flat $1,985.9m against $18,865.8m of cash and investments, and the current ratio is 4.13x [F187][D432][F180].
Buybacks and dividends of $3,808.9m consumed 93.3% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D436][D437][D459].
The FY2025 total includes a first dividend of $370.3m alongside $3,438.6m of repurchases [X140][X137].
Operating margin has fallen four years running, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].
The decline is structural, not cyclical: EYLEA US sales are shrinking on competition and the profit mix is shifting to collaboration income [P10][P9].
The revenue basis break matters: FY2018 is $5,145.6m in the table versus $6,710.8m as first reported, so growth spanning those years mixes presentations [F3][X3][R2].
Return on average equity of 14.9% ranks in the 25th percentile of eight peers against a 38.7% median, reflecting the cash-heavy balance sheet [D439][D784][D785].
US EYLEA sales: a further decline from $2,747.8m in FY2025 would confirm the erosion, while stabilisation would reverse it; watch the FY2026 10-K [S43].
Operating margin: a move back above the 34.6% window median would signal the cost trend has turned; a print below the 24.9% FY2025 low would extend it [D751][F30].
R&D at 40.8% of revenue is the window high; a rise above it would pressure margin further, a fall toward the 34.6% median would relieve it [D420][D760].
